paragraphs.source_en: Tokugawa Ieyasu’s mother had earlier come from Edo to Fushimi, where she was spending her final years in peace. All manner of people came to visit her every day.

paragraphs.source_en: The old lady had once been called Odai; now people addressed her as Lady Dentsūin.

units.source_en: The old lady had once been called Odai; now people addressed her as Lady Dentsūin.

paragraphs.source_en: Nearly all the figures who inhabited her dreams had now departed this world: Ieyasu’s father Hirotada, her mother Kayōin, her father Mizuno Tadamasa, and Sakai Uta-no-suke, who had cared for her in so many ways—

units.source_en: Nearly all the figures who inhabited her dreams had now departed this world: Ieyasu’s father Hirotada, her mother Kayōin, her father Mizuno Tadamasa, and Sakai Uta-no-suke, who had cared for her in so many ways—

paragraphs.source_en: Sixty years later, when she looked again at all that surrounded her, she often found it incredible and would secretly laugh to herself. The Takechiyo of those days had now risen to the highest rank among men and become the one who directed the affairs of the realm. As his mother, she was proud of her son. Was this wrought by human hands, or ordained by heaven? She often asked herself that question.

paragraphs.source_en: Kiyonobu, the former head of the Chaya house, had once told her, “My lady, you are the greatest mother in all the realm.” Strangely, the words had not surprised her. Whenever she recalled them, heat coursed through her entire body. Kiyonobu too had passed from this world, and the present head of the Chaya house was nineteen-year-old Kiyotada.

paragraphs.source_en: Odai’s vow had been answered. Ieyasu now bore an immense mission: to create the age of peace for which all the people longed.
